headline: Car wash changes at 101 Elm Street sent to committee; $462,755 police station loan tabled.
summary: Four public hearings covered two second-hand dealer license requests, a car wash special permit change, and a special permit at 220 Moody Street. The two license requests and the car wash change were sent to committee, and the Moody Street hearing was continued to December 14. Members also approved firefighter retirement resolutions, two Council on Aging appointments, grants, and a $120,000 truck purchase, and tabled a $462,755 police station loan.
decisions: Referred the second-hand license at 1275 Main Street for Hitz and Holos to the licenses and franchises committee.
Referred the second-hand license at 550 Winter Street for Roadshow Concepts LLC to the licenses and franchises committee.
Referred the Prestige Car Wash special permit change at 101 Elm Street to committee and recessed the hearing to December 14, 2026.
Continued the special permit hearing for 220 Moody Street until December 14, 2026.
Placed on file the mayor's request for councilors to serve on the rink design committee.
Referred the request for $42,536 for preliminary design of the Firewall Street bridge repair to the finance committee.
Referred the request for $56,760 for expanded work on the Chester Brook culvert at Beaver Street to the finance committee.
Referred the request for $40,000 for professional services from Leanne Lwazinski to the finance committee.
Approved 10 resolutions honoring retiring firefighters.
Confirmed the appointment of Richard Pizzi Jr. to the Council on Aging, 12 in favor.
Confirmed the appointment of Marsha McCleary to the Council on Aging, 12 in favor.
Approved $120,000 from the cemetery sale of lots and graves account for a new truck with snowplow for the cemetery division.
Approved accepting a $52,152 grant for the FY 2027 municipal road safety program.
Approved accepting a $9,000 grant for new EV chargers in city public parking lots.
Approved the ordinance on pay for personnel costs tied to the election, 12 in favor, after third reading.
Tabled the $462,755 loan order for design of the fire administration wing at the police station after first reading.
Approved the fortune teller license at 24 Crescent Street for Manu Park.
Approved renewal of extended hours at 12 Harvard Street for CVS pharmacy number 114.
Approved the McDevitt 8th grade civics resolution.
Approved a request asking the mayor to place a solar trash and recycling compactor on Moody Street.
Approved the 1725 petition at 205 Second Avenue for National Grid.
Approved the 1725 petition at South Street and Vernon Street for National Grid.
Granted leave to withdraw without prejudice the special permit application at 287 Crescent Street, 12 in favor.
discussion: The Prestige Car Wash request at 101 Elm Street drew questions about the new facade and roof, whether new pay stations would speed up the line, how the site would operate during construction, and whether a large sign would be removed.
Discussion of the Elm Street site also raised cracked sidewalks, standing water near the driveways, and possible tree planting. Members asked for answers in committee.
A representative for Roadshow Concepts said the business wants an annual license to hold monthly appraisal events, and questions covered its show schedule.
The 220 Moody Street hearing was recessed because an appraisal of a potential easement was still pending. The petitioner said it expected to have it within about a week.
